# E0503: two error types

Code raises one error type. Declare one type with a variant for each failure, or convert one error into the other where they meet.

- Rule: [`effects.one-error-type`](../../reference/12-effects.md#effects.one-error-type)
- Reported at: the call or `raise` that raises the second error type.
- Tier: `core`, checked in the `types` phase

## Example

This program makes the mistake:

```stilt E0503:5
type ParseError = | Empty

fn parse(text: str) -> i64 / raise<ParseError> {
  if text == "" { raise Empty }
  raise "not a number: {text}"
}
```

This one is fixed:

```stilt
type ParseError = | Empty | NotANumber(str)

fn parse(text: str) -> i64 / raise<ParseError> {
  if text == "" { raise Empty }
  raise NotANumber(text)
}
```

## What the compiler prints

`stilt check` on [`E0503_two_error_types.lt`](../../tests/diagnostics/E0503_two_error_types.lt):

```text
── TWO ERROR TYPES ─────────────────────── E0503_two_error_types.lt:5:3  [E0503]

This raises `str`, but the same code raises `ParseError`:

  5 │   raise "not a number: {text}"
    │   ^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^

Code raises one error type. Declare one type with a variant for each failure, or
convert one error into the other where they meet.
```
